The geographic distribution of healthcare indicators and specialized medical resources across Denmark reveals significant variations at both the regional and local cluster levels. These disparities highlight differences in disease incidence, quality of care metrics, and the availability of specialized practitioners depending on where patients are located.

One key area of geographic variation is the incidence of stroke (apoplexy). A national map broken down by health clusters ([[sundhedsklynger]]) shows that stroke incidence ranges from as low as 0%–0.8% in some areas to over 2.8% in others [^src1]. This data, tied to [[Indikator 5]], encompasses a wide array of local clusters, including [[Sundhedsklynge Bornholm]], [[Sundhedsklynge Byen]], [[Aarhusklyngen]], and [[Randersklyngen]], demonstrating that the burden of cardiovascular events is not evenly distributed across the country [^src1]. 

Performance on clinical development goals also varies geographically. At the regional level, the proportion of patients meeting specific targets ranged from 87.2% in [[Region Hovedstaden]] to 90.7% in [[Region Nordjylland]] [^src2]. When zooming in on the cluster level, several clusters in North and Central Jutland successfully meet these development goals, whereas the clusters with the lowest performance levels—hovering around 85%—include [[Sundhedsklynge Bornholm]] and [[Sundhedsklynge Byen]] [^src2]. Overall, the variation at the cluster level for these indicators sits between 0.5% and 1.1% [^src3].

Beyond clinical outcomes, the geographic distribution of specialized healthcare infrastructure shows stark contrasts. The availability of private practicing cardiologists ([[Praktiserende kardiologer]]) is heavily concentrated in the capital region. [[Region Hovedstaden]] hosts 13 specialist cardiology practices, whereas [[Region Midtjylland]] has only 2, and [[Region Nordjylland]] has just 1 [^src4]. This uneven distribution of specialized medical resources may have implications for patient access to specialized cardiovascular care outside the capital area.
